items.text: Northwind Cache 4.2.0 is now available on the public download mirrors and via npm (@northwind/cache). This release focuses on stability: we fixed a race condition in the eviction queue that could surface under sustained write load, and the background reaper now backs off correctly when the disk is under pressure. The memory footprint on 64-bit platforms is roughly 8% smaller thanks to a reworked slab allocator. Documentation and a migration guide for the two deprecated options (legacyTtl and strictMode) are on the project wiki. Thanks to everyone who filed reports during the release-candidate window; the changelog links each fix to its issue.

items.text:
Draft abstract and summary for the submission to the Journal of Applied Meteorology. I've kept the framing neutral so it fits either the short paper or the extended version.

We compare three downscaling pipelines for summer precipitation over the eastern slopes of the Cascades between 2005 and 2022. The baseline statistical method (quantile mapping on ERA5 predictors) and a convolutional model are benchmarked against a new hybrid that uses the neural network only to correct residuals from the statistical step. Across all 14 gauge stations, the hybrid reduces mean absolute error by 11% relative to the baseline and by 4% relative to the pure neural approach, with the largest gains at high elevations where gauge coverage is sparse.

We also report that skill degrades sharply when training windows shorter than eight years are used, which suggests that previous negative results in this region may reflect data scarcity rather than method. The discussion section should acknowledge that our neural baseline was tuned on half the stations and only lightly validated on the other half.

Remaining work: two figures (spatial error maps and a station-level scatter plot), a table of hyperparameters in the appendix, and a sentence in the acknowledgements thanking the water district for the 2019 gauge dataset. Target date for the internal draft is the 18th.

Release notes for Lumen PDF Toolkit 2.6.0, prepared for the docs site.

What's new:
- Batch conversion now runs in a worker pool, cutting wall-clock time by roughly half on files over 200 pages.
- New --flatten-forms flag for the CLI and the corresponding flattenForms option in the Node bindings.
- Font subsetting now handles variable fonts without dropping axes.

Fixes:
- Corrected a crash when the input PDF had an empty metadata dictionary. (Thanks, @dharlow.)
- Page rotation is preserved when splitting with odd page counts.
- The OCR step no longer misreads the letter O as zero in the serial field on scanned invoices from Ferro Supply; this was a very specific report but the fix is general.

Known issues:
- Very large bookmarks trees (>10k entries) can slow the first open; a fix is planned for 2.6.1.
- The Windows installer still shows the old logo in Add/Remove Programs.

Upgrade notes: no breaking API changes. If you pinned to 2.5.x for the legacy rendering path, that path now emits a deprecation warning on every call; set quietDeprecations to true if your logs are noisy.
Reference desk will be short-staffed Saturday; the self-checkout kiosks and the automated hold shelf remain open during regular hours.
